knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Radical Function Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=7{x}^{2}-9x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=14x-9.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (14x-9) \\  & =\frac{14x-9}{2\sqrt{7{x}^{2}-9x}} \\  & =\frac{14x-9}{2\sqrt{7{x}^{2}-9x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{-{x}^{2}+65}$ at the point where $x=1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=-{x}^{2}+65.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-2x.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-2x) \\  & =-\frac{2x}{2\sqrt{-{x}^{2}+65}} \\  & =-\frac{x}{\sqrt{-{x}^{2}+65}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(-\frac{x}{\sqrt{-{x}^{2}+65}})|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{-2(1)}{2\sqrt{-(1{)}^{2}+65}} \\  & =\frac{-2}{2\sqrt{64}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
